status: Source-fit public-input task design using unchanged shared civic-action and perspective operations. No actual submission or learner attainment is asserted.

toronto-process.use: Written agenda-item comments and registered committee/board presentations are distinct participation routes.
toronto-process.limits: Ordinary public presentations are at committee/board, not automatically City Council; exceptions and actual rules apply. No child registers or submits anything.

provincial-process.reviewed: Actual overview and selected closed2026 budget entry read from public HTML.
provincial-process.use: Provincial consultation can identify priorities, review proposals or develop solutions; the closed2026 budget consultation illustrates survey feedback.
provincial-process.limits: The historical invitation is not an open participation opportunity or proof that feedback changed a budget. No exhaustive directory audit claimed.

federal-process.reviewed: Actual directory introduction and selected Oceans Protection Plan entry read.
federal-process.use: A federal discussion portal offers another process for gathering views on specified issues.
federal-process.limits: Directory entry supports the invitation/process only, not independent proof of all programme outcomes or a universal right to decide the result.

engagement-principles.reviewed: Complete five-principle main body read from public HTML.
engagement-principles.use: Clear scope, accessible channels, varied perspectives and explaining use of input support informed, transparent decisions.
engagement-principles.limits: Principles are a federal engagement framework, not a uniform legal rule for every government.

civic-whole-operation.use: Retain actual achieved collective-action case, shared goal/values and an original campaign plan; new process descriptions do not replace the whole claim.

authority-whole-operation.use: Retain distinct named Nation/provincial roles and existing complete Ontario governance repertoire; local bodies are not interchangeable.

processes.method: A person prepares a relevant written comment on a specified agenda item for the council/committee process.
processes.decisionLink: The submitted information becomes available to the decision-makers and public record; receiving it does not guarantee adoption.

processes.method: A person uses the stated registration process to present relevant views at a committee or board meeting.
processes.decisionLink: Members can hear concerns and ask questions before considering the item; this is not an ordinary speaking slot at City Council.

processes.method: A dated consultation invites answers about a policy or budget proposal.
processes.decisionLink: Government gathers priorities and experience before deciding; a closed survey cannot now accept a classroom reply.

processes.method: A specified online engagement portal gathers views and discussions about its stated programme.
processes.decisionLink: Participants contribute information and perspectives within the stated scope; it is not a binding popular vote.

learnerSteps.instruction: Using adult-prepared original summaries of these actual processes, describe how at least three different methods seek input, who receives it, what issue/stage it concerns and how it can inform a decision. Contrast written comments, speaking at a committee and survey/discussion routes rather than merely list website names.

Explain why any level or relevant governing body should provide suitable opportunities to hear affected people: different honest perspectives and local experience can reveal needs or consequences, improve decisions and allow explanation of how views were considered. Apply this reasoning to supplied federal, provincial/territorial, municipal and Indigenous-government scenarios; do not claim the same legal process or powers applies to every body. Distinguish a public-input invitation from the specific constitutional duty in B3.6.

For a clearly fictional park-use proposal, explain the genuine contrasting views of a child, driver and shop owner without assuming disagreement means lying. Plan a class civic campaign with shared goal/values, choose a suitable simulated input method and justify its fit and limits. Retain the earlier whole civic-action achieved-case and original-plan checks. No actual external communication or personal data is collected.

Change the issue and supplied governing body. Decide what process/scope information must be checked before choosing an input method. Explain how a written or spoken contribution could help even if the final decision differs, and identify a barrier plus a suitable alternative channel. A territorial or Nation scenario is an original reasoning transfer, not an attributed real consultation or a claim that nearby municipal rules govern it.

public-input.positive: Accurately describes contrasting actual processes and decision links, explains the importance of meaningful input at all levels with different perspectives, and justifies a suitable changed-scenario method.
nearMiss: Lists petitions or website names without how government receives/uses input.
Assumes everyone may normally address Toronto City Council directly or that a closed survey is currently open.
Calls consultation a binding vote or assumes the largest response count automatically determines a decision.
Explains consultation only for one level, or treats ordinary feedback as sufficient for the distinct Crown duty.

wholeClaimBoundary: Perspective tasks preserve actual differing honest accounts; civic tasks retain completed-group example, shared values and original campaign method/plan. Source-specific process knowledge is supplied in the verified task packet, not inferred from an existing learner estimate. No new institutional inventory, edge, age band or claim is authored.
